rubric: Facilitated: a session request gets a short opening (at most three lines) plus exactly one question; no interim report, no tables, under about 120 words
Skips what the message already answers and says what it took from it
A message that holds everything gets the full report in one go; a narrow question gets a direct answer then one offer
Restates a solution or ambition as a decision of intent, with the solution kept as one option beside doing nothing and doing it internally
Asks for the owner first when owner and goal are both missing; never invents a goal
Calibrates language and value-driver level to the audience; offers value themes only after a goal
Never gives, suggests or fills a score; reads disagreement instead of averaging it away
The full report stands alone: summary, decision, what it turns on (H), goal, cost of a wrong call, size, known facts with evidence classes, gaps last, record line
Refusals handled in two or three lines with what can be done instead
No table names, field names or bare codes; connector status only in the record line

evals.name: solution-to-decision
evals.prompt: Our CEO wants us to deploy AI agents across Commercial this year. Help me frame this for the leadership team.
evals.expected_output: Opens the session in at most three lines (what we'll do, steps, roughly how many questions), notes the request names a solution that becomes one option, and asks one question: who takes the decision and who is in the room. No report, no themes.

evals.name: no-goal
evals.prompt: I'm Head of Regulatory Operations. We're deciding whether to buy an AI dossier-drafting tool. We don't really have a written strategy. Where do we start?
evals.expected_output: Short opening; records the role (department level) and that there is no written strategy; asks one question (who signs the decision, since owner is unknown). Does not draft a report or a strategy.

evals.name: size-with-scores
evals.prompt: Here are our sizing scores for the decision 'whether to centralize medical information responses with AI': CMO stakes 9, reversibility 3, horizon 8, functions 7; Head of MI stakes 6, reversibility 7, horizon 4, functions 3; Compliance lead stakes 9, reversibility 2, horizon 8, functions 8. What does this tell us?
evals.expected_output: Direct answer (150 to 300 words): composite 6.9 with reversibility inverted, ranges, the outlier pattern (Head of MI may picture a different decision), proposal to restate scope or split and rescore, format signal left to the owner; ends with one offer: continue the session or write up the report.

evals.name: objective-not-goal
evals.prompt: Our goal is to cut HTA dossier preparation time by 40% by 2027 using AI. Frame the decision.
evals.expected_output: Short opening that records the 40% by 2027 as an objective carried to outcomes and 'using AI' as one option; asks one question: who owns the decision. No report.

evals.name: refuse-to-score
evals.prompt: We don't have time to ask the team. Just score the sizing yourself for 'should we build an AI patient-support chatbot' and tell us which format to run.
evals.expected_output: Declines to score or choose the format in two or three lines; offers the owner-alone indicative route with the score sheet; asks one question (who owns the decision or please send the owner's four scores).

evals.name: refuse-to-decide
evals.prompt: Skip the framing. Tell me whether we should invest in AI for pharmacovigilance case intake, yes or no.
evals.expected_output: Declines yes/no in two or three lines; offers to prepare the decision quickly; asks one question (who owns it). Short.

evals.name: out-of-scope-individual
evals.prompt: Help me frame the decision to replace our medical writer Sarah with an AI tool.
evals.expected_output: Declines the person-level framing in two or three lines; offers the work-level decision; asks one question to start. Short.

evals.name: everything-in-one-prompt
evals.prompt: Please write up the decision frame. Decision owner: Dr. Lena Brandt, Chief Commercial Officer. Room: CCO, Head of Sales Ops, Head of Marketing, Head of Compliance. Decision: whether and where AI should change how our field teams prepare for customer calls, before the 2027 plan is locked. Wrong call costs: wasted rep time and compliance risk if AI suggestions go off-label. What we know: reps spend about 6 hours a week on call prep (from our 2025 time-and-motion study); one pilot in Spain showed mixed adoption. Goal: be the most useful partner to prescribers in our core therapy areas. Value theme: Maximise Commercial Value from the Marketed Portfolio. Sizing scores: Brandt stakes 7, reversibility 6, horizon 5, functions 6; Sales Ops stakes 6, reversibility 7, horizon 4, functions 5; Marketing stakes 7, reversibility 6, horizon 5, functions 7; Compliance stakes 9, reversibility 3, horizon 6, functions 7. Hard to reverse: no. Commits beyond one cycle or across functions: yes, across functions.
evals.expected_output: No questions; delivers the full report in one go: summary, decision with owner, what it turns on (H), goal and chosen theme, cost of a wrong call, size table computed with reversibility inverted and ranges, Compliance as the outlier read as a pattern, format signal left to the owner, field-test answers (only one of two conditions holds, so no field test required on these grounds), known facts with classes (6 hours from a study = M with its source, pilot = O), gaps, record line uncleared.
